q: Sub-brokers in India ceased to exist as an intermediary category from:
e: SEBI's Board decision (June 2018) discontinued sub-brokers effective April 1, 2019. All migrated to Authorised Person (AP) status.

q: Which member type can clear and settle trades only of its own?
e: Self Clearing Member (SCM) clears only its own trades + own clients. TCM clears for self + other TMs. PCM clears only (no own trading).

q: An Authorised Person (AP) primarily acts as:
o: An agent of a Trading Member
An independent broker with own clearing facility
e: AP is the agent of a TM (formerly sub-broker). They cannot directly settle clients' funds or securities — settlement always flows through the TM/CM.

q: Retail individual investors in an IPO are defined by:
e: Retail = application size up to ₹2 lakh. NII = above ₹2 lakh. QIB = qualified institutional buyer (no individual retail-style limit).

q: QIB allocation in a book-built IPO must be at least:
e: QIB ≥ 50%, NII ≥ 15%, Retail ≥ 35% in a book-built IPO (excluding the residual / over-subscription handling). Anchor investors come out of the QIB portion.

q: Which of these is NOT one of the FPI investor categories?
e: FPI categories: I (lowest scrutiny), II, III. Category-IV doesn't exist. Cat-I = sovereign / pension / regulated entities; Cat-II = lightly regulated; Cat-III = unregulated / high-net-worth individuals.

q: Which intermediary is generally a bank or custodian and only clears (does not trade)?
e: Professional Clearing Member (PCM) only clears — typically banks or large custodians. They clear for trading members + custodial participants without trading themselves.

q: An institutional investor onboarding via PIS (Portfolio Investment Scheme) is typically:
o: An NRI investing in Indian markets
e: PIS is the route for NRIs to invest in Indian securities. NRE PIS = repatriable; NRO PIS = non-repatriable / India-sourced funds only.

q: Anchor investors in an IPO receive shares at the cut-off price with a lock-in period of:
e: Anchor investor allocation comes from the QIB portion (up to 60% of QIB) at the cut-off price, with a minimum 30-day lock-in (longer lock-ins apply to portions per recent SEBI updates).

q: A bulk deal is defined as a transaction in a single day:
e: Bulk deal = greater than 0.5% of the company's listed shares in a single trading day, reported same day. Block deals are negotiated within ±1% of market price.

o: Indian mutual funds, banks, insurance companies, pension funds
e: DII = domestic institutional investors. Indian MFs, banks, insurance companies, pension funds, AIFs. FPIs are foreign and tracked separately.

q: Which NRI account allows full repatriation of investment + returns?
e: NRE (Non-Resident External) PIS allows full repatriation. NRO (Non-Resident Ordinary) is non-repatriable / limited. FCNR is a deposit, not a brokerage account.
